{{lang|zh-hans|崔永熙}} | image = | caption = Yongxi playing with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in 2024. | position = [[Shooting guard]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 5 | weight_lb = 190 | league = | team = [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] | number = 24 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2003|5|28|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Yulin, Guangxi]], China | high_school = | college = | draft_year = 2024 | career_start = 2022 | years1 = 2022–2024 | team1 = [[Guangzhou Loong Lions]] | years2 = {{nbay|2024|start}} | team2 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024]] | team3 = →[[Long Island Nets]] | years4 = 2026–present | team4 = [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] | highlights = * 2× All-[[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]] Domestic Second-Team (2023, 2024) * CBA All-Star (2024) * CBA All-Star Rookie (2023) * CBA Rookie of the Year (2023) * CBA All-Star Rookie Challenge MVP (2023){{cite web|title=Cui and Zou named MVP on first day of 2023 CBA All-Star Weekend|url=https://english.news.cn/20230325/8ce32f1f3b6646cf837afa6a2a871712/c.html|website=News.cn|publisher=Xinhua|date=25 March 2023|access-date=21 September 2024}} | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|CHN}}}} {{Medal|Competition|[[Basketball at the Asian Games|Asian Games]]}} {{Medal|Bronze|[[Basketball at the 2022 Asian Games|2022 Hangzhou]]|[[Basketball at the 2022 Asian Games – Men|Team]]}} }} '''Cui Yongxi''' ({{lang-zh|t=崔永熙}}), also known as '''Jacky Cui''' (born 28 May 2003), is a Chinese professional [[basketball]] player who plays for the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]]. He is also a member of the [[China men's national basketball team]]. Yongxi previously played for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] during the [[2024–25 NBA season]] where he only appeared in five regular season games. ==Early life== Cui was born in Guangxi, China, to Cui Mingguang, one of the most prolific street basketball players in Southern China. He initially attended, as a 16-year-old, the [[Basketball Without Borders]] camp, representing his home country and making a name for himself.{{cite web|title=BWB Global Camper Cui Yongxi inspired by ''Mamba Mentality''|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/bwb-global-camper-cui-yongxi-inspired-by-mamba-mentality|website=FIBA.com|date=24 March 2020|access-date=21 September 2024}} Afterwards, he attended the [[NBA Academy]] in [[Canberra]], graduating at 18 years old while setting his sights on going pro.{{cite web|first=Ersin|last=Demir|title=Yongxi Cui Scouting Report|url=https://edemirnba.substack.com/p/yongxi-cui-scouting-report|website=Substack.com|date=8 June 2024|access-date=21 September 2024}} ==Professional career== ===Guangzhou Loong Lions (2022–2024)=== Cui began his professional career with the [[Guangzhou Loong Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]]. In his rookie season, he played in 43 games and averaged 12.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.8 steals in 30.8 minutes.{{cite web|title=Yongxi Cui Player Profile|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Yongxi-Cui/Summary/150520|website=RelaGM.com|access-date=21 September 2024}} In his second year, Cui played 56 games and improved his numbers across the board, averaging 15.7 points, 6 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.7 steals, and 0.3 blocks per game in 34.5 minutes while shooting 45.5 percent from the field and 36.4 percent from 3, earning CBA Domestic Second Team honors.{{cite web|title=Xinjiang forward Abdusalam wins CBA MVP award|url=https://english.news.cn/20240408/0cec06235b644a97ab4853717a6aa44d/c.html|website=News.cn|publisher=Xinhua|date=8 April 2024|access-date=21 September 2024}} After the season ended, he declared for the NBA draft.{{cite tweet|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|title=NEWS: Yongxi "Jacky" Cui, a graduate of the NBA Global Academy, has entered the 2024 NBA Draft, he announced. Cui, a 6'7, 20-year old wing, is averaging 15.9 points, 5.7 rebounds and 3.1 assists, while shooting 37% from 3 for Guangzhou in the Chinese CBA.|number=1783592310795653288|user=DraftExpress|date=25 April 2024|access-date=21 September 2024}} ===Brooklyn / Long Island Nets (2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Cui joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS ANNOUNCE NBA 2K25 SUMMER LEAGUE 2024 ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-announce-nba-2k25-summer-league-2024-roster|website=NBA.com|date=5 July 2024|access-date=21 September 2024}} and on 20 September, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Chinese Forward Cui Signs NBA Contract With Brooklyn Nets|url=https://www.barrons.com/news/chinese-forward-cui-signs-nba-contract-with-brooklyn-nets-fdebe32a|website=Barrons.com|date=20 September 2024|access-date=21 September 2024}}{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Yongxi Cui to a Two-way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-yongxi-cui-to-a-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=20 September 2024|access-date=21 September 2024}} With his debut on 27 October against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Cui became the first Chinese player since [[Mengke Bateer]] to play in the NBA while going undrafted, as well as the seventh overall Chinese player to play in the NBA.{{Cite news |date=28 October 2024 |title=Brooklyn Nets' Cui Yongxi becomes seventh Chinese man to play in NBA |work=Olympics |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/brooklyn-nets-cui-yongxi-becomes-seventh-chinese-player-nba}} On 13 December, it was announced he would miss the rest of the season after suffering a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] on his left knee while playing for the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite web|title=Cui Yongxi Medical Update|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/cui-yongxi-medical-update|website=NBA.com|date=13 December 2024|access-date=14 December 2024}} On 15 December, he was waived by the Nets.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Complete Trade With Golden State Warriors|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-complete-trade-with-golden-state-warriors|website=NBA.com|date=15 December 2024|access-date=15 December 2024}} ===Return to CBA (2026–present)=== On 30 August 2025, Cui returned to China and joined the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]].{{cite web|url=https://baijiahao.baidu.com/s?id=1841862207400154408&wfr=spider&for=pc|title=崔永熙官宣加盟广东男篮|work=baidu.com|date=August 30, 2025|access-date=August 31, 2025}} ==National team career== Cui played for the [[China men's national basketball team]] during the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] and the next year he played in the Asia Cup qualifiers.{{cite web |date=20 February 2024 |title=Chinese men's basketball team announces Asia Cup qualifiers roster |url=https://www.shine.cn/sport/2402201553/ |access-date=21 September 2024 |website=Shine.cn|publisher=Xinhua}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA
